To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) tau is secreted in a regulated, activity‐dependent manner from healthy, mature neurons; 2) extracellular tau is phosphorylated differently from tau inside neurons; 3) AMPA‐inducible tau release is calcium‐dependent, and 4) tau release is dependent upon pre‐synaptic release mechanisms.
neuronal activity and calcium regulate the release of tau from healthy mature neurons, and that this is a process that could be dysregulated to lead to the spread and propagation of tau pathology.
stimulation of neuronal networks in vitro induces release of extracellular tau, which can propagate tau pathology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how tau is secreted by neurons.
the mechanisms that underpin tau propagation, and the role that tau plays in neurodegeneration.
the mechanisms of tau release from neurons, the regulation of this process, and the implications for tau pathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data presented in this study demonstrate that tau can be released from neurons in a regulated manner.
the release of extracellular tau from healthy neurons is a calcium‐regulated, activity‐dependent, physiological process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show for the first time that tau is released by neurons and this release is dependent on synaptic activity and calcium.
tau release is a regulatable process that is triggered by neuronal activity, and that it may play a role in the trans‐synaptic propagation of tau pathology.
the physiological release of tau is a regulatable process and dysregulation of this could lead to the propagation of tau pathology in neurodegeneration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tau is secreted by neurons in a regulatable process that can be modulated by synaptic activity.
tau release from healthy neurons is a regulatable process and is dependent on neuronal activity and calcium influx.
tau is released from neurons in a regulated manner, and the mechanism by which it does so involves calcium‐dependent release of vesicles from pre‐synaptic neurons.
